'''Albert Celades López''' (born 29 September 1975) is a Spanish former professional [[association football|footballer]] who played as a [[defensive midfielder]]. He is currently a [[Manager (association football)|manager]].

A tactically astute player with a strong defensive mentality, he was best known for his stints with [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] and [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/01a2-0e6b319e8fee-9843f2b769ce-1000--salad-days-for-celades/|title=Salad days for Celades|publisher=UEFA|first=Andy|last=Hall|date=26 October 2004|access-date=21 April 2010}}</ref> and he amassed [[La Liga]] total of 223 matches and eight goals over 12 seasons, totalling ten major titles with the clubs.

Celades appeared with the [[Spain national football team|Spain national team]] at the [[1998 FIFA World Cup|1998 World Cup]]. He worked as a [[Manager (association football)|manager]] after retiring, mainly with [[Spain national youth football team|Spain's youth sides]].

==Club career==
Born in [[Barcelona]], [[Catalonia]], Celades – who left Barcelona at age seven with his family to live in [[Andorra]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.metrofanatic.com/story.jsp?ID=5093|title=Media day with Albert Celades|publisher=Metro Fanatic|date=16 March 2009|access-date=22 March 2009}}</ref>– was a product of [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]]'s youth system. He made his debut with the main squad during [[1995–96 La Liga|1995–96]], and finished his first professional season with 16 games and two goals as the [[Catalonia|Catalans]] finished third in [[La Liga]]. Nevertheless, he would still spend another full campaign with [[FC Barcelona Atlètic|the reserves]].

Celades played 36 matches in [[1997–98 La Liga|1997–98]], mostly as a [[sweeper (association football)|sweeper]],<ref>{{cite news|url=http://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/1998/01/23/pagina-16/1393853/pdf.html|title=La zaga sufre más, pero encaja menos|trans-title=Back-four suffer more, but concede less|newspaper=[[Mundo Deportivo]]|first1=Eduardo|last1=Polo|first2=Joan|last2=Poquí|language=es|date=23 January 1998|access-date=13 May 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/1998/04/04/pagina-12/393895/pdf.html|title="Me quedo"|trans-title="I'm staying"|newspaper=Mundo Deportivo|first1=Manuel|last1=Segura|first2=Eduardo|last2=Polo|language=es|date=4 April 1998|access-date=9 June 2020}}</ref> as the [[Louis van Gaal]]-led team claimed the national title after a three-year drought.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://spherasports.com/el-primer-barca-de-van-gaal-parte-i-llegada-y-planificacion/|title=El primer Barça de van Gaal (parte I): 1997, llegada y planificación|trans-title=The First Barça of van Gaal (part I): 1997, arrival and planning|publisher=Sphera Sports|first=Francisco Javier|last=Roldán|language=es|date=3 March 2017|access-date=22 January 2026}}</ref> He also started both legs of the [[1997 UEFA Super Cup]], helping to a 3–1 aggregate victory over [[Borussia Dortmund]],<ref name=RSSSF>{{cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/ec/ec199697.html|title=European Competitions 1996–97|publisher=[[RSSSF]]|first=James M.|last=Ross|access-date=21 January 2026}}</ref> but appeared less significantly in the [[1998–99 La Liga|following season]], with ''Barça'' renewing their domestic supremacy.

After a year with [[RC Celta de Vigo|Celta de Vigo]], Celades moved to [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]], against which he had scored the winner (1–0) in the [[1999–2000 La Liga|previous campaign]], on 28 November 1999;<ref>{{cite news|url=http://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/1999/11/29/pagina-22/428744/pdf.html|title=Celades tumba al Madrid|trans-title=Celades downs Madrid|newspaper=Mundo Deportivo|first=Antonio|last=Mínguez|language=es|date=29 November 1999|access-date=13 May 2013}}</ref> he featured sparingly over four seasons, but added two league trophies and the [[2001–02 UEFA Champions League]] to his ''[[résumé]]''.<ref name=GlasgowValencia>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/real-madrid/2019/12/13/5df29457268e3e884c8b460a.html|title=Zidane-Celades: de Glasgow a Valencia|trans-title=Zidane-Celades: from Glasgow to Valencia|newspaper=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|first=Miguel Ángel|last=Rodríguez|language=es|date=13 December 2019|access-date=21 January 2026}}</ref> He also spent [[2003–04 Ligue 1|2003–04]] on loan to [[Ligue 1]] side [[FC Girondins de Bordeaux|Bordeaux]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/0194-0e6a6d58a049-9c06bea61503-1000--celades-bound-for-bordeaux/|title=Celades bound for Bordeaux|publisher=UEFA|date=19 August 2003|access-date=21 April 2010}}</ref>

[[File:Albert Celades cropped.jpg|thumb|left|160px|Celades with the [[New York Red Bulls]] in 2009]]
From 2005 to 2008, Celades represented [[Real Zaragoza]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/news/01ac-0e6ce764c3c3-85539080a379-1000--celades-to-settle-at-zaragoza/|title=Celades to settle at Zaragoza|publisher=UEFA|date=29 August 2005|access-date=4 May 2022}}</ref> In his [[2005–06 La Liga|first year]], he helped the club [[2005–06 Copa del Rey|reach]] the [[Copa del Rey]] final, and would be relatively used during his tenure as the [[Aragon]]ese were relegated at the end of [[2007–08 La Liga|2007–08]], and the player was released after his contract expired.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.elperiodicodearagon.com/deportes/2008/06/30/puerta-abre-47914567.html|title=La puerta se abre|trans-title=The door opens|newspaper=[[El Periódico de Aragón]]|language=es|date=30 June 2008|access-date=22 January 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.elperiodicodearagon.com/real-zaragoza/2025/12/25/albert-celades-recuerda-fatidico-descenso-temporada-dv-124881041.html|title=Albert Celades recuerda el fatídico descenso del Real Zaragoza en la temporada {{sic|nolink=y|08–09}}: "Teníamos jugadores muy buenos, pero no éramos un equipo"|trans-title=Albert Celades remembers Real Zaragoza's fateful relegation in the 07–08 season: "We had very good players, but we were not a team"|newspaper=El Periódico de Aragón|first=Jesús|last=Chueca|language=es|date=25 December 2025|access-date=21 January 2026}}</ref> In February 2009, he went on trial with the [[New York Red Bulls]] in the [[Major League Soccer]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.soccerbyives.net/soccer_by_ives/2009/02/celades-among-the-red-bulls-new-trialists.html#more|title=Celades among the Red Bulls new trialists|publisher=Soccer By Ives|first=Ives|last=Galarcep|date=22 February 2009|access-date=22 February 2009|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924103255/http://www.soccerbyives.net/soccer_by_ives/2009/02/celades-among-the-red-bulls-new-trialists.html#more|archive-date=24 September 2015}}</ref> and, after impressing, signed in March.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/2009/03/11/futbol/futbol_internacional/espanoles_mundo/1236792934.html|title=Celades jugará en los New York Red Bulls|trans-title=Celades will play in the New York Red Bulls|newspaper=Marca|language=es|date=11 March 2009|access-date=16 March 2009}}</ref>

Celades retired from competitive football on 24 October 2009, immediately following the conclusion of [[2009 Major League Soccer season|the season]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/soccer/2009-10-23-1358300433_x.htm|title=Red Bulls MF Albert Celades to retire Saturday|newspaper=[[USA Today]]|date=23 October 2009|access-date=23 October 2009}}</ref> In early 2010, however, [[Kitchee SC|Kitchee]] from Hong Kong signed him alongside compatriot [[Agustín Aranzábal]]; they both appeared with the team at the [[2010 Lunar New Year Cup]], a mid-season exhibition tournament.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.sport.es/es/noticias/barca/20100206/celades-jugara-con-kitchee-hong-kong/print-841256.shtml|title=Celades jugará con el Kitchee de Hong Kong|trans-title=Celades will play with Hong Kong's Kitchee|newspaper=[[Sport (Spanish newspaper)|Sport]]|language=es|date=6 February 2010|access-date=19 September 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304102807/http://www.sport.es/es/noticias/barca/20100206/celades-jugara-con-kitchee-hong-kong/print-841256.shtml|archive-date=4 March 2016}}</ref>

==International career==
Celades earned four [[Cap (sport)|caps]] for [[Spain national football team|Spain]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://rfef.es/es/noticias/albert-celades-seleccionador-nacional-sub-21-cumple-40-anos|title=Albert Celades, Seleccionador Nacional Sub-21, cumple 40 años|trans-title=Albert Celades, Under-21 national team manager, turns 40|publisher=[[Royal Spanish Football Federation]]|language=es|date=29 September 2015|access-date=22 January 2026}}</ref> and was a participant at the [[1998 FIFA World Cup]] with two [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]] appearances against [[Nigeria national football team|Nigeria]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/classicfootball/matches/match=8731/index.html|title=Long-suffering Spain stunned by Oliseh sizzler|publisher=FIFA|date=13 June 1998|access-date=4 August 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120710235806/http://www.fifa.com/classicfootball/matches/match%3D8731/index.html|archive-date=10 July 2012}}</ref> and [[Paraguay national football team|Paraguay]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.soccertimes.com/worldcup/1998/games/jun19.htm|title=World Cup: Nigeria third to clinch second round|publisher=Soccer Times|first=Jerry|last=Langdon|date=19 June 1998|access-date=4 August 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303235357/http://www.soccertimes.com/worldcup/1998/games/jun19.htm|archive-date=3 March 2016}}</ref> in an eventual group-stage exit.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/soccer/world/events/1998/worldcup/news/1998/06/24/spain_bulgaria/|title=Spain beats Bulgaria 6–1 but fails to qualify|publisher=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=24 June 1998|access-date=22 January 2026|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060509061816/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/soccer/world/events/1998/worldcup/news/1998/06/24/spain_bulgaria/|archive-date=9 May 2006}}</ref> His debut was on 3 June that year, in a 4–1 [[Exhibition game#International football|friendly]] defeat of [[Northern Ireland national football team|Northern Ireland]] in [[Santander, Spain|Santander]] where he started and played the entire game.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://elpais.com/diario/1998/06/04/deportes/896911202_850215.html|title=Abundante munición para Francia|trans-title=Ammonition aplenty for France|newspaper=[[El País]]|first=Cayetano|last=Ros|language=es|date=4 June 1998|access-date=23 May 2014}}</ref>

Celades' last match consisted of 30 minutes in a 2–1 away victory over [[Bosnia and Herzegovina national football team|Bosnia and Herzegovina]] for the [[2002 FIFA World Cup qualification (UEFA)|2002 World Cup qualifiers]]. He also represented the non-[[FIFA]] [[Catalonia national football team|Catalonia side]], scoring on his debut in a 5–0 defeat of Nigeria on 22 December 1998.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://hemeroteca-paginas.mundodeportivo.com/EMD03/HEM/1998/12/23/MD19981223-004.pdf|title=Catalunya da una exhibición de fútbol y goles ante Nigeria|trans-title=Catalonia put on a show of football and goals against Nigeria|newspaper=Mundo Deportivo|first=Joan|last=Domènech|language=es|date=23 December 1998|access-date=17 November 2019}}</ref>

==Coaching career==
On 7 May 2014, after [[Julen Lopetegui]] left for [[FC Porto|Porto]], Celades was named manager of the [[Spain national under-21 football team|Spanish under-21s]] after leaving the [[Spain national under-16 football team|under-16 team]].<ref name=U21>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/under21/news/0257-0ded0da452dc-b593c8e417b7-1000--celades-takes-up-spain-under-21-reins/|title=Celades takes up Spain Under-21 reins|publisher=UEFA|date=7 May 2014|access-date=20 June 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.elconfidencial.com/deportes/futbol/2014-05-07/albert-celades-nuevo-seleccionador-sub-21_126741/|title=Albert Celades, nuevo seleccionador sub-21|trans-title=Albert Celades, new under-21 manager|newspaper=[[El Confidencial]]|language=es|date=7 May 2014|access-date=14 March 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sefutbol.com/en/official-albert-celades-takes-u21|title=OFFICIAL: Albert Celades takes on the U21|publisher=Royal Spanish Football Federation|date=7 May 2014|access-date=3 August 2018}}</ref> In October, the former lost their [[2015 UEFA European Under-21 Championship qualification play-offs|play-off]] against [[Serbia national under-21 football team|Serbia]] for entrance to the [[2015 UEFA European Under-21 Championship|2015 UEFA European Championship]], in which they would have been defending champions; the 1–2 second leg loss in [[Cádiz]] was their first in 35 games.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2014/oct/14/spain-under-21s-eliminated-serbia-european-championships|title=Holders Spain knocked out of European Under-21 Championship by Serbia|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|date=14 October 2014|access-date=14 March 2016}}</ref>

On 18 July 2018, Celades resigned from his position at the [[Royal Spanish Football Federation]] after five years managing the youth sides, also having acted as assistant to the seniors during the [[2014 FIFA World Cup|2014]] and [[2018 FIFA World Cup|2018 World Cups]] and [[UEFA Euro 2016]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.europapress.es/deportes/futbol-00162/mundial-00639/noticia-albert-celades-incorpora-cuerpo-tecnico-absoluta-mundial-brasil-20140610192212.html|title=Albert Celades se incorpora al cuerpo técnico de la absoluta para el Mundial de Brasil|trans-title=Albert Celades added to full side coaching staff for Brazil World Cup|publisher=[[Europa Press]]|language=es|date=10 June 2014|access-date=28 September 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://elpais.com/deportes/2016/05/31/actualidad/1464710610_277737.html|title=Isco y Saúl fuera de la lista de Del Bosque para la Eurocopa 2016|trans-title=Isco and Saúl out of Del Bosque's list for 2016 European Championship|newspaper=El País|first=Luis|last=Martín|language=es|date=31 May 2016|access-date=28 September 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.estadiodeportivo.com/selecciones/2018/01/24/celades-seleccion-optimista-realista-mundial-rusia/141890.html|title=Celades: "La selección es optimista, pero realista, ante el Mundial de Rusia"|trans-title=Celades: "The national team is optimistic, but realistic, regarding the Russia World Cup"|newspaper=[[Estadio Deportivo]]|language=es|date=28 January 2018|access-date=28 September 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.elespanol.com/deportes/futbol/mundial/20180617/entrenadores-mundial-llevan-pinganillo-banquillo/315718713_0.html|title=¿Por qué los entrenadores del Mundial llevan un pinganillo en el banquillo?|trans-title=Why do World Cup managers wear an earpiece on the bench?|newspaper=[[El Español]]|first=Daniel|last=Calle|language=es|date=17 June 2018|access-date=28 September 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sefutbol.com/en/albert-celades-bids-farewell-rfef|title=Albert Celades bids farewell to the RFEF|publisher=Royal Spanish Football Federation|date=18 July 2018|access-date=3 August 2018|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180924222730/http://www.sefutbol.com/en/albert-celades-bids-farewell-rfef|archive-date=24 September 2018}}</ref> On 3 August, he was appointed as assistant coach of Real Madrid, reuniting with Lopetegui after their period at the Spanish Federation.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/08/celades-joins-real-madrid-as-julen-lopeteguis-assistant-coach?pid=1394215343652|title=Celades joins Real Madrid as Julen Lopetegui's assistant coach|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=3 August 2018|access-date=3 August 2018}}</ref>

On 11 September 2019, Celades became manager of [[Valencia CF|Valencia]] following the dismissal of [[Marcelino García Toral]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.valenciacf.com/en/article/en-official-statement-albert-celades-2019-09-11|title=Official statement {{!}} Albert Celades|publisher=Valencia CF|date=11 September 2019|access-date=11 September 2019}}</ref> His first match in charge took place three days later, in a 5–2 away defeat to his former club Barcelona.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.beinsports.com/en/la-liga/video/barcelona-5-2-valencia-fati-stars-as-celade-1/1293013|title=Barcelona 5–2 Valencia: Fati stars as Celades endures miserable first match|publisher=[[beIN Sports]]|date=14 September 2019|access-date=17 September 2019}}</ref> The following week, all players refused to accompany him at a press conference ahead of the [[2019–20 UEFA Champions League|Champions League fixture]] against [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]], in solidarity with his predecessor.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.standard.co.uk/sport/football/chelsea-vs-valencia-albert-celades-plays-down-player-unrest-marcelino-exit-a4238321.html|title=Chelsea vs Valencia: Albert Celades plays down player unrest after Marcelino exit|newspaper=[[Evening Standard]]|first=Andy|last=Sims|date=16 September 2019|access-date=17 September 2019}}</ref>

Celades was relieved of his duties on 29 June 2020, with the team ranked in eighth and [[2019–20 La Liga|six games to go]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.goal.com/en/news/voro-appointed-valencia-manager-for-sixth-time-after-celades/7vphs0kiv3jl12jjaydnx08j9|title=Voro appointed Valencia manager for sixth time after Celades' sacking|publisher=[[Goal (website)|Goal]]|first=Tom|last=Webber|date=30 June 2020|access-date=30 June 2020}}</ref> On 9 January 2026, he was appointed at [[Cypriot First Division]]'s [[Pafos FC|Pafos]] on a two-and-a-half-year contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://pafosfc.com.cy/pafos-fc-appoints-albert-celades-as-head-coach/|title=Pafos FC appoints Albert Celades as head coach|publisher=Pafos FC|date=9 January 2026|access-date=9 January 2026}}</ref>

On 11 August 2026, Celades replaced [[Imanol Idiakez]] at the helm of [[Segunda División]] side [[Cádiz CF|Cádiz]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cadizcf.com/noticias/albert-celades-nuevo-entrenador-del-cadiz|title=Albert Celades, nuevo entrenador del Cádiz|trans-title=Albert Celades, new manager of Cádiz|publisher=Cádiz CF|language=es|date=11 August 2026|access-date=11 August 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.canalsur.es/noticias/deportes/futbol/cadiz-destituye-idiakez-tres-meses_1_1428345.html|title=El Cádiz prescinde de Imanol Idiakez: Celades le sustituye en el banquillo|trans-title=Cádiz release Imanol Idiakez: Celades replaces him on the bench|publisher=[[Canal Sur]]|language=es|date=11 August 2026|access-date=20 August 2026}}</ref> but was himself dismissed on 19 October, after just one win in ten matches.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cadizcf.com/noticias/comunicado-oficial-albert-celades|title=Comunicado oficial: Albert Celades|trans-title=Official statement: Albert Celades|publisher=Cádiz CF|language=es|date=19 October 2026|accessdate=19 October 2026}}</ref>

==Honours==
'''Barcelona'''
